title: Render-styling PR changed sim spawn data: bbox re-extract replaced the entire spawn pool and districts
evidence:

-# Blanchardstown (W), Howth (E). Format: south, west, north, east.
-BBOX = (53.28, -6.45, 53.44, -6.03)
+BBOX = (53.30, -6.32, 53.385, -6.08)

Worktree check at sha 6f23b31a vs parent 6657ca6: old spawn_candidates=224646, new=125860, pools not equal; old districts=121, new=52.
detail: The briefing pins "Spawn candidates/district data unchanged (gameplay semantics pin)" and allows re-extract only for the sea fix. The bbox tightening is a board-extent change that churned all sim spawn inputs, forcing the dublin_board T1 state-hash re-bless — look change coupled to sim-data change.
recommended_fix: Split the board-extent/bbox change into its own PR with explicit gameplay sign-off, or document the mock-gate ruling superseding the pin in the briefing and PR body.

title: Underlay load failure is swallowed with no log, contradicting the file's own "loud in the log" claim and the never-catch-and-ignore rule
detail: The else branch sets a flag and returns silently; no fmt.eprintfln anywhere on this path (grep of app/ confirms). Project rule: every error path recovers logged or surfaces. Shipping app degrades to fallback with zero operator-visible signal.
recommended_fix: Add fmt.eprintfln("app: %s failed to load — street-skeleton fallback", UNDERLAY_PATH) in the else branch, matching the main.odin font/sprite fallback log pattern.

title: dublin_node_block_draw logs every frame per street-far node; the "one-shot log line" comment is false in code
detail: dublin_node_block_draw runs per terminal per frame from draw_nodes → draw_building. No dedup guard exists; every street-far node emits the line at 60fps. All other app logs are setup-time one-shots (grep confirms). Also pollutes harness capture stdout.
recommended_fix: Log once per node id (e.g. a seen-bitset in Dublin_Board_Render keyed by node id), or demote to a counted summary logged at board build.

title: Two parallel nearest-street-block implementations (baked street_blocks vs runtime seg grid) that can disagree; 82% of dublin.json is unread by the game
evidence:
osm_extract.py:757-760 bakes: "# --- street-aligned blocks (the MM urban-fabric layer): every spawn
    # candidate mapped to its nearest street segment (view-only data — the
    # sim reads spawn_candidates, never this; 1:1 index-aligned with it)."
    street_blocks = build_street_blocks(spawn, arterial, local)  [snap BLOCK_SNAP_MAX_TILES = 0.6]

dublin.odin instead re-derives at runtime: dublin_seg_grid_build + dublin_node_street with DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST :: 3.0. grep 'street_blocks' --include='*.odin' → zero matches. Measured: street_blocks = 4.92MB of the 6.03MB dublin.json.
detail: The bake's stated design ("the render stays dumb") was abandoned: the renderer re-implements the lookup with different snap semantics (0.6 vs 3.0 tiles), and 125,860 baked block records ship as dead weight only Python tools read. Two sources of truth for block orientation.
recommended_fix: Pick one: either have the renderer consume the baked street_blocks (tile-keyed), or drop street_blocks from dublin.json and keep the runtime grid as the single implementation.

title: Committed bake tool defaults to a machine-specific, disposable worktree absolute path
evidence:
WT = os.environ.get("PP_WT") or "/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify"  # the packet-plumber root (PP_WT overrides)

Line 6 docstring: exec(open("/Users/moses/.herdr/worktrees/packet-plumber/packet-plumber-v2-dublin-map-beautify/.scratch/blender_board_build.py").read())
detail: The pipeline that produces the committed 9MB assets/maps/dublin_underlay.png defaults into a .herdr worktree that will be deleted after review. Future rebakes silently target a stale path; provenance of a shipped artifact depends on a transient directory.
recommended_fix: Default WT to the repo root derived from __file__ (os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) + '/../..'), keeping PP_WT as override; fix the docstring exec example.

title: Underlay baked with EEVEE (GPU renderer), no Blender version pin — "byte-stable" claim holds only on the baking machine
evidence:
scn.render.engine = 'BLENDER_EEVEE'

Lines 484-500 strip only PNG tEXt/iTXt/zTXt chunks: "strip Blender's wall-clock tEXt chunks — the committed asset must be byte-stable across re-renders". No bpy.app.version pin or check exists in the file; the raw OSM cache (.osm-cache/) is also gitignored.
detail: EEVEE output varies across GPUs, drivers, and Blender versions; stripping timestamp chunks does not make pixels reproducible. The project built rlsw precisely to avoid GPU-dependent pixels (project-context: "bit-identical on every machine"). Re-bake ≠ byte-identical asset.
recommended_fix: Pin the Blender version (assert bpy.app.version at script start, record it in dublin.json extract note), or bake with a software renderer path; document the accepted reproducibility bound.

title: DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST=3.0 is unreachable: the 3×3 1-tile-cell search window only sees ~1–2 tiles
detail: Cells are 1 tile; a segment 1.5–3 tiles away never intersects the 3×3 window, so nodes within the documented radius falsely hit the axis-aligned fallback (and the per-frame log). Constant documents behavior the search cannot deliver.
recommended_fix: Either widen the window to ceil(DUBLIN_SEG_MAX_DIST) cells, or set the constant to the window's true reach (~1.5) and fix the log message.

Removed consumer (diff, dublin.odin old step 4): "- // 4. the spawn candidates (the 1-in-6 dotted texture — the gallery's\n- //    density knob at the user's blessed calm default)." — grep shows no remaining reader of b.render_dots outside core/map.odin.

title: Mock-gate scaffolding (topology/pucks/halos/blobs/LOD/tilt renders, ~half the file) committed inside the production asset bake
evidence:
# the tilted hero — at ZOOM-OUT state (the user's ruling: at zoom-out you see
# the clusters + the backbone, not individual buildings): blobs + backbone +
# circle markers, tilted.
def set_zoomout_state():
    set_vis(building_objs, False)
    set_vis([lm_ob], False)
...
# ------------------------------------------------------------- THE ASSET ---
...
def set_base_only():
    set_vis(building_objs, False)
    set_vis([lm_ob], False)
    for pair in link_ob.values():
        set_vis(list(pair), False)
detail: The shipped asset path calls set_base_only(), hiding every mock object; yet each bake run still constructs buildings, routers, pucks, halos, blobs, last-mile links and renders 5 extra LOD/tilt images into .scratch. Complexity doesn't match the production need.
recommended_fix: Split the one-time mock/topology renders into a separate mock script; keep blender_board_build.py as the lean base-map asset bake.

title: prep_board_geometry.py main() re-implements layout_clusters' seed-selection math inline
evidence:

    cands = asset["spawn_candidates"]
    pool = []
    for i in range(0, len(cands), 6):

title: PIL-based preview renderer moved into tools/blender_board/ though it uses no Blender; street-width constants restated in three places
evidence:
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont   # (no bpy import in this file; the old tools/render_dublin_preview.py was deleted)

dublin.odin:235-236 fallback widths are inline magic numbers:
		aw := max(1, i32(0.065 * v.tile_px * v.scale + 0.5))
		lw := max(1, i32(0.03 * v.tile_px * v.scale + 0.5))
(The diff deleted the named DUBLIN_STREET_ARTERIAL_W/LOCAL_W constants; prep_board_geometry.py ROAD_W = 0.065 and preview ARTERIAL_W_TILES = 0.065 restate the same value.)
detail: A pure-PIL mock tool living under blender_board/ misleads about its toolchain; the fallback street widths lost their named constants and are now triplicated across render code and tools — drift changes only the degraded fallback.
recommended_fix: Move render_dublin_preview.py back to tools/; restore named constants in dublin.odin and reference the single width value in tool comments.

title: Dublin block path inverse-transforms screen center back to tile coords instead of receiving the node's integer tile position
detail: The world pass derives c from an integer tile position, then the Dublin branch divides it back through the camera to feed the street lookup. Works only because to_screen is pure translate+scale; any camera rotation silently breaks block orientation.
recommended_fix: Pass the node's tile position (or the [2]i32 node_pos) into draw_building's Dublin branch and drop the dublin_screen_tile inverse.
